walkthrough:
Use velocity continuity at $t = 8\text{ s}$ to determine constant $k$:
$$30.6 - 0.9(8) = \frac{1600}{8^2} + 8k$$
$$23.4 = 25 + 8k \implies 8k = -1.6 \implies k = -0.2$$

Find the stopping time at $X$ by setting $v = 0$ for $t \geq 8$:
$$\frac{1600}{t^2} - 0.2t = 0 \implies 0.2t^3 = 1600 \implies t^3 = 8000 \implies t = 20\text{ s}$$

Integrate velocity across all three time intervals to determine distance:
$$s_1 = \int_0^2 7.2t^2\,dt = \left[2.4t^3\right]_0^2 = 2.4(8) = 19.2\text{ m}$$
$$s_2 = \int_2^8 (30.6 - 0.9t)\,dt = \left[30.6t - 0.45t^2\right]_2^8 = 216 - 59.4 = 156.6\text{ m}$$
$$s_3 = \int_8^{20} (1600t^{-2} - 0.2t)\,dt = \left[-\frac{1600}{t} - 0.1t^2\right]_8^{20} = -120 - (-206.4) = 86.4\text{ m}$$

Sum the distances to find $OX$:
$$OX = 19.2 + 156.6 + 86.4 = 262.2\text{ m}$$

Step 1: Use velocity continuity at the boundary $t = 8\text{ s}$. The velocity from the second phase must match the velocity from the third phase:
$$v_2(8) = 30.6 - 0.9(8) = 30.6 - 7.2 = 23.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$v_3(8) = \frac{1600}{8^2} + k(8) = \frac{1600}{64} + 8k = 25 + 8k$$
$$25 + 8k = 23.4$$
$$8k = 23.4 - 25 = -1.6$$
$$k = -\frac{1.6}{8} = -0.2$$

Step 2: Find the time when the particle comes to instantaneous rest at $X$ ($v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $t \geq 8$):
$$\frac{1600}{t^2} - 0.2t = 0$$
$$\frac{1600}{t^2} = 0.2t$$
$$0.2t^3 = 1600$$
$$t^3 = \frac{1600}{0.2} = 8000$$
$$t = \sqrt[3]{8000} = 20\text{ s}$$
